newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Asia imports 500,000 bpd WAf crude in 1H-Vitol.
newsitem.headline: Asia imports 500,000 bpd WAf crude in 1H-Vitol.

text.p: Asia imported 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) of West African crude in the first half of 1997, Ian Taylor, president of the Vitol Group of Companies, said on Monday.
He told an oil conference that tighter specifications for oil products and rising refinery capacity were supporting the demand for West African crudes.
Taylor's estimate would indicate that imports of West African grades slowed in the second quarter of 1997.
London tanker-broker Simpson, Spence & Young estimated in May that Asian arrivals in the first quarter amounted to 855,000 bpd, five percent higher than in 1996.
Crude demand normally slows in the second quarter of the year from the first.
Taylor did not offer a year-earlier comparison to his own estimate.
But he said the biggest buyer in the region was South Korea at 29 percent of imports, followed by India at 25 percent, China at 20 percent and Taiwan at 11 percent.
Taylor said more West African was flowing into Asia because Atlantic Basin crude production was rising, making more West African imports available.
But competitive pressure would also require Asian refiners to check out other crude types.
"As Asian refiners come under more margin pressure they would have to be more sophisticated and look at new crudes," to maximuse yields, he said.
West African crudes are generally relatively low in levels of sulphur, the kind of oil Asian refineries have a big appetite for.
Taylor said that under the current configuration of Asian refiners, the region could import 1.0 to 1.2 million bpd.
However, higher levels of imports would mean the region would be under-utilising secondary unit capacity, which makes higher premium and low-sulphur products.
